title: Slompret Synthesizer
exhibition: Arai Eek Colabs — Chiang Mai, Thailand
description: Slompret is an experimental electronic instrument inspired by the traditional East Javanese blowing instrument of the same name, often crafted in the form of a dragon's head. Reinterpreting the relationship between breath, sound, and mythology, the project transforms this folk instrument into a DIY electronic synthesizer driven by a CMOS CD4093 circuit. By combining Southeast Asian cultural heritage with open-source hardware practices, Slompret explores the intersection of folklore, experimental music, and collaborative making, creating new possibilities for cultural transmission through contemporary electronic sound. Developed within a DIWO (Do It With Others) framework, the project is supported by openly accessible hardware documentation, schematics, and assembly guides, enabling others to learn from, modify, and build upon the instrument through its public repository.

title: Mecucu Sensor
description: Mecucu is an electronics workshop module designed around a simple wind-activated switch. Named after the Javanese word mecucu, meaning "to pout," the project draws inspiration from the gesture of blowing to create interaction. Participants learn the fundamentals of electronic circuits through hands-on experimentation, using breath as an intuitive interface to control DC-powered devices. By transforming a simple bodily action into an electronic trigger, Mecucu offers an accessible introduction to electronics while encouraging playful engagement with technology.

title: Cicadra — Insect Synthesizer
description: Cicadra is a hands-on electronic sound workshop developed as part of the Persami project by Waft Lab for the Rokko Meets Art festival in Kobe, Japan. Inspired by the distinctive soundscape of Japanese summer, participants build a cicada-shaped synthesizer based on a simple NE555 oscillator circuit while exploring the fundamentals of electronic sound generation. Through assembling, modifying, and experimenting with the instrument, the workshop introduces basic principles of oscillation and sound design in an accessible and playful way, encouraging participants to engage with technology through making, listening, and creative exploration.

title: Pinarax Workshops
description: Pinarak is a participatory media art workshop developed in collaboration with Waft Lab that draws inspiration from local rituals to foster environmental awareness through collective creative action. Bringing together art, nature, and community engagement, the project invites participants to take part in a series of collaborative activities that reinterpret traditional practices through contemporary media art. Through hands-on making, performance, and shared experiences, Pinarak encourages participants to develop a deeper connection with their surrounding environment while exploring how cultural knowledge and collective creativity can contribute to ecological stewardship and social change.

title: TITEN Installation Art Workshop
description: TITEN Installation Art Workshop was a three-day educational program introducing participants to the fundamentals of installation art through discussion, collaborative design, and hands-on concept development. Bringing together artists, makers, and installation art practitioners, the workshop explored contemporary installation practices while encouraging participants to develop their own site-specific ideas. Through group brainstorming sessions, concept presentations, and critical discussions, participants learned how to translate artistic concepts into spatial experiences, culminating in the presentation of schematic proposals for original installation artworks.

title: Oprex Budoyo
description: Awikworks Oprex Budoyo is a dynamic workshop and multimedia installation that channels the vibrant energy of East Javanese subculture to foster an open, collaborative artistic community. Rooted deeply in the traditional art of Bantengan, the project translates this rich cultural heritage into a contemporary context by adopting a self-sufficient electronic approach built entirely from PCBs and customized electrical components. This synthesis of past and present highlights how traditional artistic objects can organically evolve beyond conventional boundaries when fueled by a shared do-it-yourself spirit. By combining various communal activities and integrating an immersive, Bantengan-inspired soundscape composed by TamaT, the installation transforms into a joyful cultural event that not only sustains the historical creative energy of the region but also resonates profoundly with the modern zeitgeist.

title: Jiwo Ketok Simulator
description: Jiwo Ketok Simulator is a collaborative workshop project created with Penahitam that explores S. Sudjojono's concept of jiwo ketok (the visible soul of the artist). Using a self-built electronic drawing device, participants generate marks through touch and interaction, allowing expression to emerge directly from bodily engagement. By merging DIY electronics, drawing, and collective experimentation, the project reimagines Sudjojono's ideas within a contemporary participatory framework, where the trace of touch becomes a manifestation of presence, intention, and individual character.

title: 24 Hours Workshop Service
description: 24 Hours Workshop Service is a hands-on introductory PCB-making workshop developed in collaboration with Bajra Warehouse and Petong Art House. Participants are invited to create their own visual compositions directly on printed circuit boards while learning the fundamentals of electronic circuits and component assembly. Balancing creative freedom with technical constraints, the workshop challenges participants to follow a functional electronic schematic while expressing their individual artistic ideas. Through this process, 24 Hours Workshop Service transforms circuit-making into an accessible and playful learning experience that bridges art, design, and basic electronics.

title: Circuit Bandrex
description: Circuit Bandrex Workshop was a collaborative program between Bajra and the New Media Art Creation course at the Department of Art and Design, Universitas Negeri Malang. The workshop introduced participants to the practice of circuit bending, encouraging them to creatively modify low-voltage electronic devices to produce unexpected sounds, visual outputs, and experimental sonic behaviors. Through hands-on exploration, participants learned the fundamentals of electronic circuits while embracing chance, improvisation, and playful experimentation, transforming everyday electronics into unique instruments for audiovisual expression.

title: Si Mini Muni
description: Si Mini Muni is a hands-on electronic sound workshop developed by Bajra Warehouse that introduces participants to the creative potential of piezoelectric buzzers through simple circuit-making and playful experimentation. Using accessible electronic components and found materials, participants assemble small sound devices capable of transforming everyday objects into unexpected musical instruments. The workshop emphasizes learning through making, encouraging participants to explore the relationship between electronics, sound, and materiality while discovering how simple circuits can generate a wide range of sonic possibilities.
